text:
customer-admin: Hey team — after our corp proxy firmware update yesterday, our Private/VPC endpoint (app.private.redwood:443) started failing for some customers. Java 8 clients on Windows get SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert: handshake_failure. curl from the same host returns 'SSL: no shared cipher'.

mike-support: Thanks — can you paste the exact errors and a minimal repro command? Also which proxy appliance and firmware version?

customer-admin: Error from app logs: "javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert: handshake_failure". Repro from affected host: 
```
> curl -v https://app.private.redwood/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://app.private.redwood/health
*   Trying 10.20.30.5...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to app.private.redwood (10.20.30.5) port 443 (#0)
* schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80090331) - The token supplied to the function is invalid.
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80090331) - The token supplied to the function is invalid.
```

Also tried OpenSSL from a linux jumpbox: 
```
> openssl s_client -connect app.private.redwood:443 -servername app.private.redwood -tls1_2
CONNECTED(00000003)
140205283017456:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unsupported protocol:s23_clnt.c:782:
---
no peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 0 bytes
---
```

mike-support: Ok that output suggests the proxy (or LB) is actively refusing TLS1.2/older handshakes or there is no compatible cipher overlap. Which JRE build is the client running? Are you terminating TLS at the proxy (TLS termination) or passing through to backend?

customer-admin: Clients are on Oracle JRE 1.8.0_181 (Windows). Proxy is AcmeCorp LB v12.4. We thought it was passthrough but infra says the LB terminates TLS and re-encrypts to backend.

priya-eng: Common root causes here: 1) Proxy TLS profile set to TLS1.3-only or a narrow cipher list (no RSA/ECDHE-RSA ciphers). 2) Server cert is ECDSA-only while Java8's schannel/OpenJDK combo on Windows expects RSA ciphers by default. 3) SNI mismatch causing the LB to present a different cert/profile.

mike-support: Action items to triage quickly:
- From a failing client run these (paste outputs):
```
# OpenSSL client test forcing TLS 1.2 and a couple ciphers
openssl s_client -connect app.private.redwood:443 -servername app.private.redwood -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256'

# curl forcing TLS1.2 and specific ciphers
curl -v --tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' https://app.private.redwood/health

# For Java (quick check) run with system props to force TLS1.2 and RSA ciphers
java -Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.2 -jar your-client.jar
```
- Ask your infra team for the LB TLS profile (cipher list) and whether it's using an ECDSA cert or RSA.
- Provide a tcpdump from the client host for the failed handshake if possible: `tcpdump -w /tmp/hs.pcap -s 0 host app.private.redwood and port 443`

customer-admin: Ran the openssl command with several ciphers. Output shows no cipher negotiated and the LB returns immediately: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect lb.corp:443 -servername app.private.redwood -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256'
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = lb.corp
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=lb.corp
   i:/CN=Corp-Proxy-CA
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 5 bytes and written 295 bytes
---
```
That 5 bytes read is odd, and curl still fails with schannel errors on Windows.

priya-eng: That 5 bytes read usually means the server sent an immediate TLS alert (handshake_failure). Two likely infra fixes: 1) Enable RSA/ECDHE-RSA ciphers on the LB (some vendor "modern" profiles only offer TLS1.3 or ECDSA ciphers). 2) If the LB uses an ECDSA cert but backend clients require RSA, add an RSA cert or allow RSA ciphers. Also confirm SNI is forwarded — if the LB presents a default cert that doesn't match the SNI, the client may be rejected.

mike-support: Workaround options while infra updates LB:
- Upgrade client JRE to a newer build (JRE11+) which has better TLS1.2/1.3 interoperability.
- On Windows curl/PowerShell, switch to a curl build that uses OpenSSL (not schannel) and specify --tlsv1.2 and a supported cipher.
- If you control the client JVM, explicitly set allowed protocols/ciphers: use TLSv1.2 and a cipher suite list with RSA variants.

customer-admin: Sent LB TLS profile from infra: it was set to "modern-only" (TLS1.3 preferred, and TLS1.2 with ECDSA-only ciphers). They've switched it to "intermediate" and added the ECDHE-RSA and AES-GCM suites. After that, a quick curl from the Windows jumpbox now returns 200.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: deploy job 2026-03-17T15:32:10 succeeded (no changes to app).

mike-support: Great — can you confirm Java 8 clients also succeed or if they still need a JRE upgrade?

customer-admin: Confirmed: Java 8 clients can now connect without the system property changes. We still plan a controlled JRE upgrade but the immediate outage is resolved.

priya-eng: Follow-ups/recommendations (summarized):
- Prefer RSA/ECDHE-RSA ciphers in TLS1.2 profiles for broader client compatibility (especially older JREs and Windows schannel).
- Ensure SNI passthrough or correct cert selection on the LB.
- Long term: move clients to modern JREs (11+) and consider TLS1.3 support with fallback for legacy clients.
- If you see similar issues again, collect: `openssl s_client -connect ... -tls1_2 -cipher '...'`, `tcpdump` pcap of handshake, and LB TLS profile export.

mike-support: Marking as resolved — re-open if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
